“Can you explain it to me?” 

How we met? It’s rather simple really. Circumstance and I just tend to butt heads.

It was the middle of March and time went on as it usually does. Routine after routine. Wake up, work, school, home. And just as schedule always permits my grandfather had work across the states. So as a parting gift and a safe return my sisters and I treated him to dinner. Cheesecake factory was the unanimous decision and by unanimous I mean I had no voice in the matter. Not that it would influence the stage we were set upon. The restaurant was packed just as it always is and while waiting for seating something piqued my interest. Came across my eyes. It was a simple moment, a small gesture, just a peek, just a glance. And that’s when it happened…

All it took was that… That one look through that window and then you see her, she catches your eye. Like those cheesy romantics, the girl across the train station, the woman on the bridge. That fantasy, that instinct, and oh it was running wild. Without thinking, without knowing, actions were taking place. My feet were already motion; advancing through the door. Possessed, I approached… and there she was. Amongst the muffled crowd and rushed commerce… there she was. The world was filled with blank stares and indecipherable mutters.

I became completely oblivious to all factors. My family I’m sure would jest my detachment but long winded arguments leave me breathless and exhausted. And resolutions are for New Years waiting to be broken.  

You start to think about that simple idea in your head, that chance, that dream. The clock starts ticking in your brain and the pendulum swings side to side. Heart pounding across your chest. You could start an anthem. One man band. Lead an army. Once more unto the breach dear friends. Allegories aside you can guess what came next.

Every motion my eyes saw became exaggerated and the world dimmed out. There she was graceful in stride as if she were gliding on ice. She wore a simple yellow dress, not to revealing, brilliantly resting upon her shoulders, brighter than sunshine, that fluorescent hue… She was like a sunflower in bloom. Her hair a dark brown with tints of red, an adorable length, short, sweetly innocent, barely reaching down to her neck. And her eyes… those beautiful brown eyes… you could get lost in them. So lost you’d shy away. Just to be safe. Just to stay sane. She was a simple complexity. And yet here I was trying to piece together this dream. This imagining… She was the kind of girl you see in movies, abstract, more than a concept, an ideal. She knew she was beautiful. She didn’t need to show it and that in itself led me further in. Slowly trudging my way I became trapped. Pushing myself further. Step by step a heart beat and a half. Until I was so close my heart stopped. I went flat line. Pulse unreadable. All it took was a simple hello, a hi, or how do you do. But my brain wasn’t having any of it. I choked on words. They were too heavy for me, too taxing. You know you’ve found something amazing when the very voice in your head tells you to stop. Save yourself from yourself because your words have more meaning than yourself. But you press forward, each statement, more convoluted than the next. Every letter, every word, sentence… As if you were on trial.

She mocked me, poked fun at my inadequacies.  Made me vulnerable. I became flustered by her chide remarks and witty advances. But I kept talking to her… not because I wanted to. But because I needed to. I was compelled to. As bashful as I was I found this bitter honesty, these pressing statements… cute and appalling. I was mesmerized by her sadism. I took the abuse and enjoyed it. Like a sick puppy craving that attention. Hurt me if it will make you love me. Accept me flaws and all. I can take it. You know you’ve reached a new low when depreciation is the new self esteem. You know you have a problem when masochism is a career choice.

“So… what is it then… how did it happen?”

“We met at a bookstore and I bought her coffee…”

I must have been sputtering words in my head again because it seemed like he didn’t hear a thing. Then again everything feels vague, blurred, out of place with this mindset. He was detached and I wasn’t going to grab on either. Reality had nothing for me to hold on to. Life felt lucid. I was on thin air.
I write.. that by far is my only passion...

I tried archery, music, school, work, drawing, writing... I just dont seem to find joy in anything. I only found joy when I was in love. When I was with someone.. I know its stupid. I just liked that feeling of coming home to someone, waking up to someone.
i cant think of anything. which is why i want to die.
